S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S042.name: Low_Self_Esteem
S042.description: A persistent tendency to evaluate oneself as incompetent or worthless; chronically low self-evaluation.

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: A persistent perception that one is useless or inferior to others.
subtypes.Self-Criticism: Excessively and repeatedly blaming oneself for past minor failures or flaws.
subtypes.Reduced Self-Efficacy: Distrust in one's own ability to perform tasks or solve problems.
subtypes.Chronic Sense of Inferiority: Persistently evaluating oneself lower in comparison to others.
subtypes.Lack of Self-Assurance: Continually feeling anxious and unsure about decisions or actions.

S083.name: Hopelessness
S083.description: A feeling of despair or having no hope for the future.

subtypes.Future Hopelessness: The persistent conviction that the future holds no possibility of improvement.
subtypes.Belief in Impossibility of Improvement: The belief that the current situation will absolutely not get better.
subtypes.Helpless Resignation: A state of helplessness and resignation, believing that nothing will change despite effort.
subtypes.Chronic Pessimism: A persistent tendency to view everything negatively and fail to consider positive possibilities.

info.persona: Alex Ruiz is a detail‑oriented, compassion‑driven data analyst who balances soccer, mindfulness, and budget‑smart Spanish cooking, yet occasionally procrastinates on paperwork in favor of a good playlist; they constantly juggle structure and flexibility.
info.professional_persona: Alex Ruiz, a budding management analyst with strong Excel, SQL, and data‑visualization skills, leverages their meticulous organization and compassionate conflict‑mediation style; they streamline workflows and foster inclusive, data‑driven decision‑making in a fast‑paced corporate environment.
info.cultural_background: Alex is of Spanish descent, with family ties that emphasize close‑knit relationships, respect for tradition, and a love for communal gatherings. Growing up in a bilingual household, he fluently speaks both Spanish and English, which shapes his worldview and communication style. Spanish cultural values of hospitality, collective well‑being, and appreciation for food and festivals inform his compassionate approach to teamwork and community involvement. Living in Chandler, Arizona, Alex blends his European heritage with the multicultural environment of the Southwest, often participating in local Hispanic celebrations while also embracing the broader American culture.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In his free time, Alex balances active social pursuits with reflective solitary activities. He enjoys playing recreational soccer with a local league, which satisfies his teamwork and cooperative instincts. Hiking the desert trails around Chandler offers him structured physical challenges and a chance to unwind alone. He also loves cooking traditional Spanish dishes for family and friends, exploring the culinary heritage of his roots. Alex reads non‑fiction books on leadership and psychology, practices mindfulness meditation to maintain emotional resilience, and volunteers at a community center teaching basic computer skills to Spanish‑speaking adults.
info.sports_persona: Alex Ruiz plays as a midfielder for the Chandler Kickers in a local recreational soccer league, follows the Arizona Diamondbacks and Phoenix Suns avidly, joins a desert‑hiking club for weekend treks, and balances competitive drive with a laid‑back approach to fitness through regular yoga sessions; they thrive on team camaraderie and the solitude of desert trails.
info.arts_persona: Alex Ruiz relaxes by listening to the flamenco guitar of Paco de Lucía and the indie folk of The Lumineers, attends occasional screenings of Pedro Almodóvar films, and visits the Phoenix Art Museum to admire contemporary murals, finding that these artistic experiences sharpen their analytical creativity; they often draw parallels between rhythm and data patterns.
info.travel_persona: Alex Ruiz plans trips with a spreadsheet to maximize budget efficiency, favoring short road trips to the Grand Canyon and Sedona as well as occasional flights to San Diego, while dreaming of backpacking to Machu Picchu and exploring Barcelona’s Gothic Quarter once their MBA tuition is covered; they balance careful planning with a spontaneous urge for adventure.
info.culinary_persona: Alex Ruiz enjoys cooking intermediate‑level Spanish dishes such as paella with saffron, chorizo, and mussels, a hearty tortilla española, and refreshing gazpacho, often experimenting with fresh olive oil and smoked paprika while occasionally resorting to store‑bought broth when time is tight; they love sharing meals with friends and family as a way to nurture connections.

info.persona: Jennifer Spadaro blends a disciplined, solitary work ethic with a competitive spark, channeling their anxiety into meticulous planning, yet they often over-schedule themselves and retreat into late-night watercolor sessions to unwind.
info.professional_persona: Jennifer Spadaro, a certified elementary and middle school teacher with a physics and computer science background, designs meticulous STEAM curricula that blend coding, experimental labs, and watercolor-inspired visual projects, while they leverage their competitive drive to push student achievement metrics and mentor newcomers in low-anxiety, solitary-friendly classrooms.
info.cultural_background: Jennifer descends from a second‑generation Italian‑American family that settled in the Chicago suburbs. Her parents emigrated from southern Italy, preserving traditions such as Sunday family meals, Catholic holidays, and participation in the annual Italian heritage festival in Oak Brook. Growing up in Hickory Hills, she absorbed the Midwest’s emphasis on hard work, humility, and community involvement, while the cultural diversity of the Chicago area expanded her appreciation for varied artistic and intellectual experiences. This blend of Italian familial values and Midwestern sensibility informs her disciplined approach to teaching, her love of art and cuisine, and her preference for intimate, low‑key social settings.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In her downtime, Jennifer pursues solitary creative outlets such as watercolor painting and sketching in a personal art journal. She enjoys playing piano in a quiet corner of her home and attends occasional evening concerts at the Chicago Symphony Hall. Her curiosity drives her to read popular science books, experimental fiction, and philosophy essays. She frequently visits the Art Institute of Chicago and the Museum of Science and Industry for fresh inspiration. Jennifer also tends a small vegetable garden, practices daily mindfulness meditation to manage anxiety, and engages in birdwatching at local forest preserves. Occasionally she builds simple Arduino robotics projects in a community makerspace, channeling her competitive side into perfecting functional prototypes.
info.sports_persona: Jennifer Spadaro enjoys low-key morning jogs along the Des Plaines River Trail, follows the Chicago Cubs during baseball season and the Chicago Bulls in winter, and they are a member of the local community cycling club where they ride a vintage road bike to stay fit without the fatigue of crowded gyms.
info.arts_persona: Jennifer Spadaro spends evenings sketching in their art journal while listening to Beethoven’s piano sonatas, draws inspiration from Monet’s impressionist water lilies and Frida Kahlo’s bold self-portraits, and they regularly attend performances by the Chicago Symphony Orchestra featuring conductors like Riccardo Muti.
info.travel_persona: Jennifer Spadaro prefers meticulously planned solo trips that balance quiet exploration with cultural immersion, having recently visited the botanical gardens of Kyoto for lavender tea ceremonies, the historic streets of Florence for its Renaissance art, and they are planning a future road trip to the Upper Peninsula’s remote birdwatching sanctuaries.
info.culinary_persona: Jennifer Spadaro, a confident home cook, whips up seasonal vegetable ratatouille using garden tomatoes, zucchini, and fresh basil, perfects a Sunday family lasagna layered with ricotta and spinach, and they savor a slice of deep-dish Chicago pizza topped with mozzarella, sausage, and a dash of crushed red pepper, all while they perfect their technique at the kitchen counter accompanied by soft piano background.

info.persona: Josiah Saffouri, a 45-year-old master carpenter and folk-rock guitarist, merges sustainable woodworking with artful living, constantly worries about project deadlines, yet they find calm in garden-grown vegetables and museum strolls.
info.professional_persona: Josiah Saffouri is a seasoned residential carpenter who leverages 25 years of framing, custom cabinetry, and fine-detail woodworking expertise, blending green-building practices and digital SketchUp designs with a curious, detail-obsessed mindset that drives their transition toward a boutique studio of sculptural furniture, and they balance meticulous organization with flexible creativity while assertively managing client expectations.
info.cultural_background: Josiah grew up in a middle‑class suburban family of European descent with Mediterranean roots hinted by his surname. Raised in the New York‑New Jersey border region, he absorbed a mix of American work‑ethic values and the cultural diversity of Palisades Park, a community known for its Korean, Hispanic, and other immigrant populations. Family gatherings featured traditional American holidays alongside occasional Levantine dishes, giving him an appreciation for cross‑cultural flavors. His early exposure to his father's woodworking shop and his mother's love of museum trips nurtured his curiosity for both craft and art, shaping a worldview that values inclusivity, craftsmanship, and artistic exploration.
info.hobbies_and_interests: When not on the job site, Josiah indulges in the visual arts, often spending weekends at New York City museums and local gallery openings. He enjoys sketching design ideas, restoring vintage furniture, and playing acoustic guitar while experimenting with folk‑rock tunes. Hiking the Palisades cliffs, tending to a small vegetable garden, and exploring international cooking, especially Mediterranean recipes from his family heritage, keep him grounded. He also follows craft‑beer brewing, reads philosophy, and volunteers at community art workshops.
info.sports_persona: Josiah Saffouri hikes the Palisades cliffs each fall, is a member of the Hudson River Trails Club, plays pickup basketball on weekends while cheering for the New York Knicks, and follows the New York Giants and Yankees as their favorite professional sports teams.
info.arts_persona: Josiah Saffouri spends weekends sketching at the Met, attending gallery openings featuring emerging artists like Kehinde Wiley's studio, draws inspiration from folk-rock legends such as Bob Dylan and The Avett Brothers while playing acoustic guitar, and admires the work of Anselm Kiefer and Georgia O'Keeffe, integrating those visual and musical influences into their furniture designs.
info.travel_persona: Josiah Saffouri, who prefers meticulously planned trips, has explored Mediterranean culinary roots in Barcelona and Santorini, trekked the cliffs of Iceland's South Coast, and dreams of a future workshop tour in Kyoto, balancing their travel schedule around project deadlines and budgeting constraints.
info.culinary_persona: Josiah Saffouri, an adept home cook, blends their Mediterranean heritage with garden-fresh produce to craft dishes like grilled branzino with sumac, lamb tagine with preserved lemon, and shakshuka, while pairing each meal with a locally brewed craft IPA, showcasing their advanced cooking skills and love for bold flavors.
